The licensee moved without submitting a change in address, requesting a new site, or submitting an application for a new
license. Animal Care must be informed of any change in business address so that new locations can be approved for
regulated activities and animal welfare ensured through continued unannounced inspections. Licenses are issued to
specific persons, and are issued for specific activities, types and numbers of animals at approved sites. A licensee must
notify Animal Care prior to any change of address where regulated activity occurs and the site must be approved prior to
conducting regulated activity. Correct by submitting notification of new address no later than October 2, 2026.

citations.desc: Access and inspection of records and property; submission of itineraries.
citations.narrative:
A responsible adult was not available to accompany APHIS Officials during the inspection process at 1:45pm on 9/28/26.
When the inspector arrived, the facility, house, yard, and storage buildings were completely empty. The inspector
attempted to contact the licensee by calling and leaving a voicemail and then texting. After approximately 5 minutes of
waiting, the licensee texted back that she had moved that weekend. Failure to provide access to the facility, animals, and
records for inspection is a violation of the AWA and regulations. Continued failure to provide access is serious and may
result in enforcement action.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
End Section
